---
title: "Citation-chaining log"
last-reviewed: "2026-09-08"
---

Use this when following references backwards from a paper or following later work that cites it. Record each seed and direction so you can retrace a useful discovery.


<details class="template-copy">
<summary>Open the blank copyable template</summary>

Copy this plain-text version into your approved project record. Repeat entry fields as needed and remove prompts that do not apply. The guidance and examples below help you complete it.

```text
Citation-chaining log

Blank register

ID: C-001
Seed record: [verified citation/ID]
Why selected: [ ]
Direction: backward / forward / indirect
Resource/index: [ ]
Date: [ ]
Records found: [n]
Retained: [n + IDs]
New seeds: [ ]

Eligibility logic: [ ]
Generations or stopping rule: [ ]
Limitations: [coverage, missing citations, database differences]
```

</details>

## Check your record

Keep stable IDs for retained records and new seeds. Counts alone cannot show which sources entered the review.

## Scenario test

Two indexes return different citing sets. Record which index you used, since neither result represents every citation.
